- If sentiment is positive (≥0.20) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and forecast is rising, cap upward momentum; price may not sustain rally.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), forecast should not overshoot by more than 5% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after 80+ peak, price drops 10-15% in next 5 days), model should adjust downward with lagged smoothing.  
- If forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong upward momentum (e.g., >80% increase in 5 days), consider sentiment-driven breakout bias — adjust upward with 1-2% buffer.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, avoid linear extrapolation; incorporate sentiment decay — if sentiment drops below 0.10, reduce forecast slope by 10-20%.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is volatile, forecast should be more conservative — avoid sharp peaks or troughs unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive days of direction.
